hook: The cousin of the Prophet, fourth caliph of Islam and first imam of the Shia.

pages.x: Ali was the son of Abu Talib, the uncle who raised Muhammad, and tradition says he was born inside the Kaaba itself. When Abu Talib fell on hard times, Muhammad took young Ali into his own home, and Ali, still a boy, was one of the very first to accept Islam.

On the night Muhammad fled Mecca in 622, assassins surrounded his house. Ali, about 22, lay down in the Prophet's bed under his green cloak, so the killers would think Muhammad was still inside. At dawn they burst in and found Ali; Muhammad was already far away.

Ali married the Prophet's daughter Fatima, and their sons Hasan and Husayn were Muhammad's beloved grandsons. He was famous as a warrior, with the forked sword Zulfiqar; at Khaybar, it was said, he tore the fortress gate off its hinges and used it as a shield.

When Muhammad died in 632, some believed he had named Ali to lead after him. But the community chose Abu Bakr, then Umar and Uthman. Ali became the fourth caliph only in 656. Those who believe he should have come first became the Shia, "the party of Ali".

His five-year reign was torn by civil war, against Aisha, the Prophet's widow, at the Battle of the Camel, and against Muawiya, the governor of Syria. He ruled from Kufa in Iraq. In 661 a rebel struck him with a poisoned sword while he prayed in its mosque.

His sermons, letters and sayings were collected as the Nahj al-Balagha, "The Peak of Eloquence". One of them, from a letter to a governor of Egypt: "People are of two kinds: either your brothers in faith or your equals in humanity."

Ali is honoured by all Muslims as a cousin of the Prophet, a brave warrior and a wise judge. For the Shia, more than one in ten Muslims, he is the first imam, and his shrine at Najaf is one of their holiest places.
